title: Northern Khmer people - Wikipedia
text: Northern Khmer people or colloquially as Thais of Khmer origin; mostly referred to as Khmer Surin is the designation used to refer to ethnic Khmers native to the Isan region of Northeast Thailand.

title: Austroasiatic languages - Simple English Wikipedia, the free...
text: The Austroasiatic languages are a family of languages. They are spoken in Southeast Asia. There are 157 languages, with about 117 million speakers. The biggest group of speakers speak Khmer language or Vietnamese.

title: Khmer, Northern | Ethnologue Free
text: Northern Khmer is a stable indigenous language of Thailand. It belongs to the Austro-Asiatic language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Austroasiatic languages | Mon-Khmer, Munda & Vietic | Britannica
text: Most Austroasiatic languages, notably Khmer, Mon, Bahnar, Kuay, and Palaung, do not have tones. This is noteworthy, considering that the language families found to the north—Tai-Kadai, Sino-Tibetan, and Hmong-Mien (Miao-Yao)—all have tones.

title: Khmer, Northern | Accent Network
text: Austro-Asiatic. Khmer, Northern, Thailand.The Northern Khmer dialect uses the Khmer script, which is an abugida script written from left to right. Font requirements and typography considerations are similar to Central Khmer but may have regional variations.

title: Khmer Language - Structure, Writing & Alphabet - MustGo
text: Khmer, also known as Cambodian, belongs to the Mon-Khmer branch of the Austroasiatic language family. It is the second most widely spoken Austroasiatic language after Vietnamese.

title: Northern Khmer
text: Other comments: Northern Khmer has a decimal system. Northern Khmer, called Khmer Surin, is spoken by the Khmer native to the Thai province of Surin and nearby areas. There are about 1,400,000 speaker.

title: Austro-Asiatic languages - Academic Kids
text: Austro-Asiatic languages. The Austroasiatic languages are a large language family of Southeast Asia and India. The name comes from the Greek word for South Asia.
